title: Arch tutorial: a small house
summary: Build a small house in the BIM workbench with the sizes of the Arch tutorial: walls, doors, windows, a slab, a column, a roof and levels.

credit.changes: Words in Simplified Technical English, FreeCAD 1.1 names. The page builds a real house from a DWG plan; here a small house uses the sizes the page gives: exterior walls 25 cm, interior walls 15 cm, doors 1 m x 2.45 m and 0.70 m x 2.10 m, a 15 cm slab, a 2.25 m column. Stairs, rendering and drawings are left out.

hints: Find the workbench selector in the toolbar.
Open the list of workbenches.
Workbench: BIM.

steps.say: Push **{Arch_Wall|Wall}**. Draw the outer walls round a rectangle 8000 mm × 6000 mm from the origin. Set **Width** to 250 mm and **Height** to 2600 mm.
steps.why: Exterior walls of the tutorial are 25 cm thick.

picture.alt: Walls of the tutorial's house, on the lines of its floor plan.

hints: Click the four corners. Close the wall at the first corner.
Set Alignment so that the walls are inside the rectangle.
Corners at 0 mm and 8000 mm × 6000 mm, width 250 mm, height 2600 mm, alignment Right.

steps.say: Push **{Arch_Wall|Wall}** again. Draw an inner wall across the house at x = 4000 mm. Set **Width** to 150 mm.
steps.why: Interior walls of the tutorial are 15 cm thick.
hints: Start and stop the wall on the inner faces of the outer walls.
Use the centre alignment for this wall.
From x = 4000 mm, y = 250 mm to y = 5750 mm, width 150 mm.

steps.say: Push **{BIM_Door|Door}**. Put a door 1000 mm wide and 2450 mm high in the front wall, 1500 mm from the corner.
steps.why: A door in a wall cuts its own hole in the wall.

picture.alt: A door in a brick wall of the tutorial's house.

hints: Click on the wall to put the door in it.
Set the width and height of the door in the Tasks panel.
Door 1000 mm × 2450 mm, 1500 mm along the front wall.

steps.say: Push **{Arch_Window|Window}**. Put a window 1200 mm × 1200 mm in the front wall. Put a window 1500 mm × 1200 mm in the right wall. Set both sills to 900 mm.
hints: Use a window preset in the Tasks panel.
The sill height is the distance from the floor to the window.
Front window 1200 × 1200 mm at 5000 mm; side window 1500 × 1200 mm; sills 900 mm.

steps.say: Push **{BIM_Door|Door}**. Put a door 700 mm wide and 2100 mm high in the inner wall.
steps.why: Interior doors of the tutorial are smaller than the main door.
hints: Click on the inner wall to put the door in it.
Set the width and height of the door.
Door 700 mm × 2100 mm.

steps.say: Push **{BIM_Slab|Slab}**. Draw the floor slab under the house, 8000 mm × 6000 mm and 150 mm thick.
hints: Draw the outline of the slab on the outline of the walls.
Set the thickness of the slab, and put its top at the floor level.
Slab 8000 × 6000 mm, 150 mm thick, from z = -150 mm to 0 mm.

steps.say: Push **{BIM_Column|Column}**. Put a column 250 mm × 250 mm and 2250 mm high at x = 9500 mm, y = 1000 mm.
steps.why: The tutorial's short columns are 2.25 m high.

picture.alt: Columns of the tutorial's house, made from circles of the plan, beside the walls.

hints: Set the size of the column in the Tasks panel before you click.
Click where the column stands.
Column 250 × 250 mm, 2250 mm high, at x = 9500 mm, y = 1000 mm.

steps.say: Push **{Arch_Roof|Roof}** on the outline of the walls at 2600 mm. Set 30 deg on the long sides and 90 deg on the short sides.
steps.why: An angle of 90 deg gives a gable end.
hints: Make a closed outline at the top of the walls. Select it before you push Roof.
Set the angle of each edge in the Tasks panel.
Angles 30 deg, 90 deg, 30 deg, 90 deg, overhang 300 mm, thickness 150 mm.

steps.say: Push **{Arch_Level|Level}** for the ground floor and for the roof. Push **{Arch_Building|Building}** to put both levels in one **Building** object.
steps.why: Levels put the model in order for IFC export.
hints: Select the objects of each level before you push Level.
Select the two levels before you push **Building**.
Ground floor at 0 mm with the walls, doors, windows, slab and column. Roof level at 2600 mm.

steps.say: Done: a small house with walls, doors, windows, a slab, a column and a roof, in two levels.
